Compare Model Predictions at the Same Covariate Values

predict.bin_interaction.Rd

Apply each fitted model and its saved bin definitions to common new-data rows. Original data units must be preserved.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bin_interaction'
predict(object, newdata = object$grid$data,
  warn = TRUE, interval = c("confidence", "none"),
  level = if (is.null(object$level)) 0.95 else object$level, ...)

Arguments

object

An object returned by bin_interact().

newdata

A data frame containing each focal variable and control once. The outcome is not required. Extra columns are ignored. Defaults to the stored grid.

warn

Warn if any prediction or requested interval is unavailable. Default TRUE.

interval

Pointwise confidence intervals for the predicted mean by default. Use "none" for point estimates only.

level

Confidence level strictly between 0 and 1. Defaults to the saved level, or 0.95 for objects created before confidence intervals were introduced.

...

Reserved. Supplying additional arguments is an error.

Details

For an optional spline comparator, predictions reuse the knots and boundary knots saved during model fitting. They are not recalculated from newdata. Confidence intervals condition on the specified spline degrees of freedom; they do not account for selecting or tuning that complexity. Natural splines are linear outside boundary knots on the model link scale. Extrapolation is flagged and is not evidence of adequate support.

Each original covariate row is passed to the continuous model and separately mapped to each candidate's saved categories. Predictors are not rescaled and bins are not recalculated. Missing or nonfinite inputs, uncovered bin values, unobserved factor levels, and unavailable fits produce missing predictions with an explicit status. Rows are retained. A numeric value beyond its training range sets extrapolated to TRUE, even when the continuous model supplies a prediction. This flag checks individual numeric ranges, not joint support or causal validity.

Linear models use stats::predict.lm confidence intervals with the residual degrees of freedom and a t critical value. These use the ordinary model covariance, assuming independent errors with constant variance; exact finite sample coverage also assumes normal errors and the specified mean model. Logistic models use approximate normal Wald intervals on the logit scale, then transform both limits to probabilities with the inverse link. They use the ordinary GLM covariance and assume independent observations and a correctly specified model. Limits remain on the probability scale without symmetric clipping. Sparse data can make these approximations unreliable.

These are pointwise intervals for a conditional mean or probability, not simultaneous bands or intervals for individual future outcomes. They condition on the selected model, cutpoints, and covariate values. They do not account for bin selection, cutpoint estimation, clustering, or other dependence. A narrow interval does not establish that the functional form is correct. Failed or flagged fits have no intervals. Numerically unavailable limits are marked explicitly and do not discard otherwise usable point estimates.

Differences subtract the continuous benchmark at the identical original row. For logit these are probability differences, not log-odds or odds ratios. Multiply by 100 to express them as percentage-point differences. If the benchmark prediction is missing, its paired differences are also missing. No confidence interval or uncertainty estimate for a difference is calculated.

Value

A long data frame with model, row (the newdata row position), estimate, status, extrapolated, focal_bin (the first focal variable's category or "continuous"), lower, upper, interval_status, and difference. The lower and upper columns are confidence limits for estimate, not difference. They are NA when unavailable or not requested. interval_status is ok, not_requested, prediction_unavailable, or nonfinite_interval. Attributes interval, level, and interval_method record the interval settings and method. Prediction status is ok, missing_or_nonfinite_predictor, uncovered_by_scheme, unobserved_category, model_unavailable, or nonfinite_prediction.
